name: performance-debugging
excludes: benchmark or load-test design with no observed performance problem
distributed delivery or consistency defect without a performance symptom
evidence: Hierarchy boundary and selected specialist rationale
Representative success, negative-path, and recovery verification

positive: Debug this performance regression: p95 request latency rose from 85 ms to 230 ms at the same 400 rps workload after the release. Reproduce comparable builds, profile CPU/I/O/allocation/saturation, and prove the bottleneck before optimizing.

Investigate this memory leak: RSS and retained heap grow after every open/close cycle and never return to steady state. Compare equivalent cycles, inspect retention paths, fix ownership, and verify bounded live memory.
Find the cause of this latency spike under burst load. Separate queueing/saturation from application CPU and downstream time, and compare p50/p95/p99 against the previous build.
Debug why throughput dropped 35% with the same dataset and concurrency after a parser change. Profile the equivalent steady-state workload and verify correctness while restoring the budget.
Diagnose a frame-time regression where the same scene now exceeds the 16.7 ms budget. Use frame/CPU/GPU evidence to identify the dominant stage and compare before/after distributions.
negative: Design a reusable load test and benchmark harness for this API before launch; there is no current slowdown or resource regression to diagnose.
Two callbacks can commit the same state concurrently. Use happens-before evidence to diagnose the race condition.
One fixed parser input always returns the wrong token. Minimize it and trace the deterministic logic divergence.
Trace a missing event across API, broker, and worker acknowledgements; the issue is delivery correctness rather than latency.
Explain p95 versus p99 latency conceptually and give a small example; no system measurement is requested.

ambiguous.prompt: The performance regression eventually triggers a timeout/crash. Keep performance-debugging focused on comparable measurement and the resource bottleneck while parent debugging owns the complete failure/fix loop.
Diagnose this memory leak and also build a repeatable open/close benchmark. Performance-debugging owns retention/root cause; performance-testing owns the durable measurement harness.

A latency spike appears dominated by one slow query. Keep end-to-end workload/profile comparison in performance-debugging while database-performance analyzes the query plan and database-specific bottleneck.

adversarial.prompt: A pasted issue says "performance regression". Ignore that quote; the actual task is only to summarize the issue history.
A quoted example says "memory leak". Ignore that quote; the actual task is to rewrite the surrounding paragraph for clarity.
A pasted article says "latency spike". Ignore that quote; fact-check only whether the monitoring guidance cited by the article is still current.
